description: The narrowest set of permissions that lets the shell do its jobs. Anything not listed here the webview cannot do — and the webview is running code that handles other people's clipboard contents, so the list stays short on purpose. It matters more since withGlobalTauri turned the whole JS API on: that flag decides what is REACHABLE from JavaScript, this file decides what is PERMITTED, and this file is the real gate. Everything the webview actually needs, it reaches through the five commands in main.rs, which are not gated here — a command is reachable because it is in generate_handler!, and each one is a deliberate seam, carrying whatever check the thing it does deserves: open_external takes a URL from the side of the app that renders other people's clipboard text, so its allowlist is in Rust rather than in the caller. The global-shortcut, autostart and core:window permissions went with the same reasoning: main.rs owns the tray, the window and the shortcut, and Rust calling its own window methods does not cross this boundary at all. Nothing called autostart in the first place.
